page.layout: One page of text, one column, full width. Running head at the top with the page number at the top right. Below the running text, a rule and a centred division heading (II., APPENDIX, DE, SITV, AMPLITVDINE, Magnificentia, Portu Carthaginis.). The first paragraph after the heading opens with a woodcut initial. Catchword at the lower right, signature at the lower left. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: habitatorum & praesidiariorum in potestatem Saracenorum devenit, totaque fere diruta concidit, atque in solitudinem rediit. Nec postea resurrexit unquam, fortunaque ejus Tunetem in urbem vicinam migravit, quae jam amplissimi regni caput, & regum aut proregum sedes est. Clades illa πτυωλέθρος[?] à Saracenis ei accidit imperante Romanis Constantino Pogonato, urbis Romae anno MCCCCXXXVIII[?], qui concurrit cum aerae Christianae vulgaris anno DLXXXV, Hegirae Mahometicae LXV.
main_text.head: II. APPENDIX DE SITV, AMPLITVDINE, Magnificentia, Portu Carthaginis.
main_text.p: Carthaginis situm, amplitudi-nem, magnificentiam, por-tum nobilissimum antiquos scriptores optimos velut pe-nicillo delineare, & oculis nostris quasi subjicere, dixi. Eorum verba libet hic in gratiam lectorum adscribere.In parte ea litoralis Africae, secundum mare

page.notes: The woodcut initial C is joined to the first word, read as Carthaginis. The Greek word at the start of the continuation is hard to read; the reading is doubtful. The Roman numeral for the year 1438 looks irregular in the scan; the count of c's is uncertain. The missing space in "adscribere.In" is kept as printed. The left edge shows show-through and marks from the neighbouring page, which are not transcribed.
